_note: v2 hook overrides for le Jardin des Proverbes (B58_proverbes). Every hook describes what is actually painted (nothing is written in the paintings); idioms are acted out literally.

fr_proverbe_noun.hook: Like English 'proverb', said proh-VEHRB: a stone statue of a wise old sage in the garden holds a scroll with a PROVERB, an owl on his head and a snail nodding on the plinth.
fr_proverbe_noun.why: Reworded to match the painting: the owl on the statue's head is added; the scroll is blank (no text).

fr_avoir_le_bras_long_idiom.hook: "Have the long arm": a mayor in a tricolor sash stretches an amazingly LONG ARM right across the hedges to ring a little house's doorbell: he HAS INFLUENCE everywhere.
fr_avoir_le_bras_long_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: one doorbell on one little house is painted, not the whole town.

fr_avoir_un_poil_dans_la_main_idiom.hook: "A hair in the hand": a LAZY man dozes in a hammock; he works so little that a single hair has sprouted in the middle of his open palm.

fr_c_est_la_fin_des_haricots_idiom.hook: "The end of the beans" (ah-ree-KOH): a cook tips his pot upside down and the very last green bean falls out: ALL IS LOST!
fr_c_est_la_fin_des_haricots_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he tips the empty pot out rather than scraping it.

fr_chercher_la_petite_bete_idiom.hook: "Look for the little beast": a girl with a huge magnifying glass inspects a tiny ladybird on a perfect frosted cake: NITPICKING.
fr_chercher_la_petite_bete_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the tiny bug is a ladybird.

fr_filer_a_l_anglaise_idiom.hook: "Slip off English-style": a guest in a bowler hat tiptoes away, finger to his lips, while two ladies chat over their tea and never notice: LEAVING WITHOUT SAYING GOODBYE.
fr_filer_a_l_anglaise_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he tiptoes away from a tea party across the lawn; there is no gate behind him.

fr_mieux_vaut_tard_que_jamais_idiom.hook: A tortoise breaks the finish ribbon at midnight under the moon, and a girl, a rabbit and a squirrel cheer: BETTER LATE THAN NEVER.
fr_mieux_vaut_tard_que_jamais_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cheering crowd is painted instead of a banner (no text).

fr_il_n_y_a_pas_le_feu_idiom.hook: "There's no fire": a fireman calmly sips his tea on a bench while a snail strolls past: THERE'S NO RUSH.

fr_petit_a_petit_l_oiseau_fait_so_idiom.hook: "Little by little the bird builds its nest" (lwah-ZOH): a bluebird adds one twig at a time to its nest in a little tree: SLOW AND STEADY WINS.

fr_qui_vivra_verra_idiom.hook: "Who lives will see": a wise old owl in glasses peers at an egg in a nest: TIME WILL TELL what hatches.

fr_rome_ne_s_est_pas_faite_en_un__idiom.hook: Little builders in hard hats lay one brick at a time round a model of the Colosseum: ROME WASN'T BUILT IN A DAY.
fr_rome_ne_s_est_pas_faite_en_un__idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the model Rome is a Colosseum.

fr_ce_n_est_pas_la_mer_a_boire_idiom.hook: "It's not the sea to drink": a wave of sea water towers over a boy, but he only has to drink one glass of water: IT'S NOT THAT HARD.
fr_ce_n_est_pas_la_mer_a_boire_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the boy holds up his glass in front of a great wave.

fr_apres_la_pluie_le_beau_temps_idiom.hook: "After the rain, fine weather": the clouds part, a rainbow appears and a frog lifts its umbrella to the sun: EVERY CLOUD HAS A SILVER LINING.
fr_apres_la_pluie_le_beau_temps_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the rainbow is added.

fr_avoir_un_coup_de_foudre_idiom.hook: "A thunderbolt" (koo duh FOODR): a lightning cloud flashes over a young man and a young woman and hearts fly out: LOVE AT FIRST SIGHT.
fr_avoir_un_coup_de_foudre_idiom.why: meteo follow-up: the couple are a young man and woman.

fr_il_fait_un_froid_de_canard_idiom.hook: "Cold of a duck" (frwah duh kah-NAR): a duck in a scarf shivers by a frozen pond: IT'S FREEZING COLD.

fr_il_pleut_des_cordes_idiom.hook: "It's raining ropes": ropes pour down from a rain cloud and a boy in yellow climbs one: IT'S RAINING CATS AND DOGS!

fr_quand_les_poules_auront_des_de_idiom.hook: "When hens have teeth": one grinning hen flashes a big set of teeth among ordinary hens: WHEN PIGS FLY!
fr_quand_les_poules_auront_des_de_idiom.why: kept, matches the painting. Respelling uses 'pou' (no syllable that reads as poo).

fr_l_habit_ne_fait_pas_le_moine_idiom.hook: "The habit doesn't make the monk": a wolf in a monk's habit stands among the sheep and fools nobody: DON'T JUDGE A BOOK BY ITS COVER.

fr_c_est_du_gateau_idiom.hook: "It's cake" (gah-TOH): a boy finishes his test in a minute and has time for a slice of cake: IT'S A PIECE OF CAKE.
fr_c_est_du_gateau_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the slice of cake sits on his desk.

fr_en_un_clin_d_oeil_idiom.hook: "In a wink" (klan-DUHY): a rabbit magician winks and vanishes in a burst of sparkles: IN THE BLINK OF AN EYE.
fr_en_un_clin_d_oeil_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the rabbit is the magician, winking.

fr_vouloir_c_est_pouvoir_idiom.hook: "Wanting is being able": a determined snail has climbed to the top of a tall rock and waves its little red pennant: WHERE THERE'S A WILL, THERE'S A WAY.
fr_vouloir_c_est_pouvoir_idiom.why: R1 theater follow-up: a red pennant.

fr_faire_la_tete_idiom.hook: "Make the head" (lah-TEHT): a boy SULKS with a huge pouting head and his arms crossed.

fr_avoir_un_chat_dans_la_gorge_idiom.hook: "A cat in the throat" (shah, GORZH): a singer can't sing because a tiny kitten is peeking out of her scarf at her throat: A FROG IN ONE'S THROAT.
fr_avoir_un_chat_dans_la_gorge_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the kitten peeks out of her scarf (softened from coughing it up).

fr_couter_les_yeux_de_la_tete_idiom.hook: "Cost the eyes of the head": the price tag hanging from a lady's new straw hat shows a pair of eyes, and she clutches her cheeks in shock: IT COSTS AN ARM AND A LEG.
fr_couter_les_yeux_de_la_tete_idiom.why: R1 theater follow-up: no hat stall; the tag hangs from her hat.

fr_revenons_a_nos_moutons_idiom.hook: "Let's get back to our sheep": a teacher at a blackboard herds a flock of sheep back into class: LET'S GET BACK TO THE SUBJECT.

fr_les_doigts_dans_le_nez_idiom.hook: "Fingers in the nose": a girl breaks the finish ribbon tapping her nose with one finger, not even trying: EASILY, with no effort.
fr_les_doigts_dans_le_nez_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: she taps her nose (softened from picking it).

fr_mettre_son_grain_de_sel_idiom.hook: "Put in your grain of salt": a busybody shakes salt into a gardener's soup, adding her two cents where nobody asked: SHE CHIPS IN WITH AN OPINION.
fr_mettre_son_grain_de_sel_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: one bowl of soup is painted. Gloss and English example reworded: the usual English equivalent trips the content filter (no 'butt'/'kill' wording); meaning unchanged.
fr_mettre_son_grain_de_sel_idiom.en: to put in one's two cents' worth (unasked)
ex: Il faut toujours qu'il mette son grain de sel !
He always has to put in his two cents' worth!

fr_appeler_un_chat_un_chat_idiom.hook: "Call a cat a cat": a blunt judge in a wig points straight at a ginger cat on a stool: CALL A SPADE A SPADE.

fr_mettre_la_main_a_la_pate_idiom.hook: "Put your hand in the dough": a baker kneads while lots of hands reach in to help: PITCH IN AND HELP!

fr_faire_d_une_pierre_deux_coups_idiom.hook: "Make two hits with one stone": a boy throws one stone and knocks down two cans at once: TWO JOBS DONE IN ONE GO.
fr_faire_d_une_pierre_deux_coups_idiom.why: kept, matches the painting. Gloss and English example reworded: the usual English equivalent trips the content filter (no 'butt'/'kill' wording); meaning unchanged.
fr_faire_d_une_pierre_deux_coups_idiom.en: to do two things at once (two birds, one stone)
ex: En allant au marché, je fais d'une pierre deux coups.
By going to the market, I get two jobs done at once.

fr_faire_la_grasse_matinee_idiom.hook: "Make the fat morning": a boy SLEEPS IN, snoring in a bed out on the grass ("grahs") under the roses while the sun is already high.
fr_faire_la_grasse_matinee_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the bed stands on the grass under a rose pergola and the sun is high.

fr_voir_la_vie_en_rose_idiom.hook: A girl looks through pink rose glasses and everything looks pink: SEEING THE BRIGHT SIDE.

fr_avoir_la_peche_idiom.hook: "Have the peach" (lah-PEHSH): a girl bites a peach and bounces in the air, FULL OF ENERGY.

fr_etre_comme_un_poisson_dans_l_e_idiom.hook: "Like a fish in water" (pwah-sohn dahn LOH): a grinning fish leaps happily in the fountain: it FEELS TOTALLY AT HOME.
fr_etre_comme_un_poisson_dans_l_e_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the fish is in a fountain, not a bowl.

fr_etre_dans_la_lune_idiom.hook: "Be in the moon": a boy sits on a crescent moon above the roses, chin in hand: DAYDREAMING.

fr_avoir_la_chair_de_poule_idiom.hook: "Hen's flesh" (shair duh POUL): a shivering woman has goosebumps all over her arms, just like the white hen beside her: GOOSEBUMPS.
fr_avoir_la_chair_de_poule_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: a whole hen stands beside the shivering woman. Respelling uses 'pou' (no syllable that reads as poo).

fr_avoir_la_tete_dans_les_nuages_idiom.hook: "Head in the clouds": a boy walks along with his head up inside a cloud and doesn't see the tree ahead: ABSENT-MINDED.
fr_avoir_la_tete_dans_les_nuages_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he walks toward a tree, not a lamp post.

fr_avoir_une_faim_de_loup_idiom.hook: "A wolf's hunger": a wolf in a napkin sits beside a tall stack of empty plates: STARVING!

fr_ne_pas_etre_dans_son_assiette_idiom.hook: "Not in your plate": a sad man sits outside his giant empty dinner plate: FEELING UNDER THE WEATHER.

fr_avoir_le_cafard_idiom.hook: "Have the cockroach" (kah-FAR): a gloomy cockroach sits at a café table with a coffee under its own little rain cloud: FEELING DOWN.
fr_avoir_le_cafard_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the rain cloud is added.

fr_etre_aux_anges_idiom.hook: "Be with the angels": a girl hugs her new puppy on a cloud among smiling cherubs: OVERJOYED.

fr_tomber_dans_les_pommes_idiom.hook: "Fall into the apples": a man swoons into a heap of apples: HE FAINTS.

fr_casser_les_pieds_idiom.hook: "Break the feet" (kah-say lay PYAY): a pest stamps on a man's feet and the man yelps: he ANNOYS everyone.
fr_casser_les_pieds_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: one man yelps as the boy stamps.

fr_avoir_du_pain_sur_la_planche_idiom.hook: "Bread on the plank": a baker carries a plank piled high with loaves: SO MUCH WORK TO DO.

fr_avoir_le_trac_idiom.hook: An actor freezes on the bandstand with STAGE FRIGHT, knees knocking like a train on a TRACK ("TRAHK").
fr_avoir_le_trac_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the stage is the bandstand.

fr_poser_un_lapin_idiom.hook: "Put down a rabbit": a girl waits at a café table with only a rabbit on the chair opposite: she's been STOOD UP.

fr_donner_sa_langue_au_chat_idiom.hook: "Give your tongue to the cat": a boy shrugs and sticks his tongue out toward a cat: I GIVE UP GUESSING.
fr_donner_sa_langue_au_chat_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he sticks his tongue out at the cat (softened from handing it over).

fr_se_creuser_la_tete_idiom.hook: "Dig your head": a puzzled man scratches his head while a tiny gardener digs on top of it with a spade: RACKING HIS BRAINS.
fr_se_creuser_la_tete_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: a tiny gardener does the digging.

fr_couper_la_poire_en_deux_idiom.hook: "Cut the pear in two": two children each hold one half of a pear: MEET HALFWAY.

fr_avoir_les_yeux_plus_gros_que_l_idiom.hook: "Eyes bigger than the belly": a skinny boy stares up at a towering cake he could never finish: BITE OFF MORE THAN HE CAN CHEW.
fr_avoir_les_yeux_plus_gros_que_l_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the cake towers in front of him.

fr_avoir_le_coeur_sur_la_main_idiom.hook: "Heart on the hand": a kind girl holds out a glowing heart in her hand to an old man: VERY GENEROUS.

fr_tourner_autour_du_pot_idiom.hook: "Turn around the pot": a man keeps walking round and round a big pot on the campfire and never gets to the point: BEATING AROUND THE BUSH.

fr_mettre_les_pieds_dans_le_plat_idiom.hook: "Feet in the dish": a boy steps right into a dish of spaghetti: PUT YOUR FOOT IN IT!
fr_mettre_les_pieds_dans_le_plat_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the dish is spaghetti.

fr_raconter_des_salades_idiom.hook: "Tell salads": a storyteller juggles lettuces while he spins his tales for the children: TALL TALES!
fr_raconter_des_salades_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he juggles lettuces (softened from lettuces flying out of his mouth).

fr_il_ne_faut_pas_vendre_la_peau__idiom.hook: "Don't sell the bear's skin before you've caught it": a seller holds up a bear-shaped fur coat while a very much alive bear grins right behind him: DON'T COUNT YOUR CHICKENS BEFORE THEY HATCH.
fr_il_ne_faut_pas_vendre_la_peau__idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: there is no hunter; the seller holds a bear-shaped coat.

fr_mettre_la_charrue_avant_les_bo_idiom.hook: "The plow before the oxen": a farmer scratches his head because his plow stands in front of his two baffled oxen: PUTTING THE CART BEFORE THE HORSE.

fr_sauter_du_coq_a_l_ane_idiom.hook: "Jump from the rooster to the donkey": a chatty frog leaps from a rooster over to a donkey: CHANGING THE SUBJECT abruptly.
fr_sauter_du_coq_a_l_ane_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the frog leaps between them.

fr_tirer_les_vers_du_nez_idiom.hook: "Pull the worms from the nose": a detective with a magnifying glass watches a smiling worm wriggle out of a stone statue's nose: WORMING OUT INFORMATION.
fr_tirer_les_vers_du_nez_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: the suspect is a stone statue head and one friendly worm comes out.

fr_etre_sur_son_trente_et_un_idiom.hook: "On your thirty-one": a gentleman in a tuxedo stands proudly on top of a tall stack of hatboxes: DRESSED TO THE NINES.
fr_etre_sur_son_trente_et_un_idiom.why: Reworded to match the painting: he stands on hatboxes (no number is painted).
